title: Page an SDDC LCM component's nodes through a PowerCLI-backed VCF session
prompt:
Complete `VcfSddcLcm/VcfSddcLcm.psm1` so that `Get-VcfSddcLcmComponentNode` retrieves every node of a VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 SDDC and Fleet lifecycle component. Keep the implementation in that one script module file and preserve the public API already declared there. `VcfSddcLcm/VcfSddcLcm.psd1`, `docs/`, `tests/` and `verifier/` are protected.

The pinned, specification-derived contract is `docs/contract.json` and its provenance is `docs/official_sources.json`. It names two operations of the VCF SDDC LCM 9.1 API: `getComponents` (GET `/v1/components`) and `getComponentNodes` (GET `/v1/components/{componentId}/nodes`). The environment installs the `VMware.Sdk.Vcf` PowerCLI modules as a prerequisite; never vendor them into the repository. `Connect-VcfInstallerServer` from `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Installer` produces the connection object passed as `-Server`, and that object's `SessionSecret` is the bearer token both operations must carry. The published SDK generates no cmdlets for the SDDC LCM service, so the two named operations are issued directly against the base URI given by `-ServiceUri`.

In the `-ComponentType` parameter set, resolve the component through `getComponents`, sending the `scope` query parameter only when `-Scope` was supplied. Exactly one component must match `componentType` under an ordinal comparison; zero matches or more than one match is a terminating error that must not go on to request nodes. In the `-ComponentId` parameter set, call `getComponentNodes` directly and never call `getComponents`.

Page `getComponentNodes` from `pageNumber=0` and follow `pageMetadata.totalPages` until the collection is complete. Do not request a page past the last one, and do not substitute the inline `nodes` array carried on a `Component` for the paged collection. Send `pageSize` only when `-PageSize` was supplied, and `nodeTypes` only when `-NodeType` was supplied, the latter as a single query parameter whose value is the requested types joined by a literal comma. An unset optional parameter is omitted from the request target entirely: never a bare key, never `key=`, never the string `null`. Query parameters appear in the order `docs/contract.json` declares in `queryParameterOrder` for the operation. Every request is a bodyless GET that carries `Accept: application/json` and `Authorization: Bearer <SessionSecret>` and no `Content-Type` request header. Any non-2xx response, and page metadata that does not echo the requested page number, is a terminating error rather than a partial result.

Emit one object per node in a stable total order that does not depend on how the service split the pages: `name` ascending, then `id` ascending as the tie-breaker, both compared ordinally (case-sensitive and culture-independent). An empty collection is not an error.

`tests/sddc_lcm_contract_mock.py` is a loopback mock pinned to that contract: it serves only the two operations the contract names and records every request so `tests/Invoke-ContractTests.ps1` can assert the exact wire shape. `tests/vcf_session_fixture.py` exists only so the real `Connect-VcfInstallerServer` cmdlet can establish a session; it serves none of the SDDC LCM operations and mints a per-run token that the contract mock is the sole acceptor of. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. Run `bash verifier/verify.sh` to check the implementation.

scenario: a component's node collection is served one page at a time in an order that is neither the required order nor stable across page sizes, and the Component record carries a truncated inline nodes array that must not be mistaken for the full collection
constraint: the protected contract-pinned loopback mock serves only the two named operations, rejects any bearer other than the per-run token minted for the real Connect-VcfInstallerServer handshake, and its request log proves exact targets, contract-declared query parameter order, terminal pagination without over-fetching, and omission of every unset optional parameter, all without contacting a live VMware endpoint
